title: Semantic and accessible HTML
summary: Structure a page, landmarks, headings, actions, forms, and media for browsers, search engines, keyboards, and screen readers.

lessons.title: Document anatomy and semantics
lessons.concept: HTML describes content nature and hierarchy, not appearance. The browser turns elements into a DOM tree and an accessibility tree, so correct elements provide meaning before any CSS. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

explanation.title: Mental model
explanation.text: HTML describes content nature and hierarchy, not appearance. The browser turns elements into a DOM tree and an accessibility tree, so correct elements provide meaning before any CSS. explanation.title: Simple analogy
explanation.text: Tags are building signs: main, nav, and footer identify area functions before decoration.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: doctype activates standards mode; html carries language; head contains metadata and body rendered content. Correct language improves pronunciation and assisted translation. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: header, nav, main, and footer create navigable landmarks. A page normally has one main, while a section should have a heading describing its theme. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: Heading levels h1–h6 express document nesting rather than visual size. A logical outline lets people scan a page without reading every paragraph. Finally apply the concept through one small isolated change, check the result, and revert if needed. Short changes make cause and effect easy to connect.

lessons.title: Links, buttons, and keyboard navigation
lessons.concept: A link changes resource or URL; a button triggers an action in the current context. Native elements automatically provide focus, keyboard activation, role, and name that handmade JavaScript rarely reproduces completely. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

explanation.title: Mental model
explanation.text: A link changes resource or URL; a button triggers an action in the current context. Native elements automatically provide focus, keyboard activation, role, and name that handmade JavaScript rarely reproduces completely. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

explanation.title: Simple analogy
explanation.text: A door goes elsewhere like a link; a switch acts within the room like a button.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: href gives a link its destination, enables opening in a new tab, and works without JavaScript. A fake onClick link removes those capabilities. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: button responds to Enter and Space; type=button prevents accidental form submission. aria-expanded exposes panel state and aria-controls names its target. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: Focus order normally follows the DOM. Avoid positive tabindex; keep controls visibly focused and move focus logically when a dialog opens or closes. Finally apply the concept through one small isolated change, check the result, and revert if needed. Short changes make cause and effect easy to connect.

explanation.title: accessible name
explanation.text: Text assistive technology uses to identify a control.

explanation.title: focus
explanation.text: Current target receiving keyboard actions.

explanation.title: state
explanation.text: Changing information such as open, selected, or disabled.

explanation.title: General application
explanation.text: Choose the native element by action outcome, then test the whole journey with Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, and Escape.

explanation.title: Application to L’ecomax
explanation.text: Categories are links; opening filters, adding to cart, and closing a modal are buttons whose state must be announced.

explanation.title: Expected result
explanation.text: Evidence of success: Tab reaches each control in order, Enter activates links, Space activates the button, and expanded state changes.

lessons.title: Useful images, tables, and metadata
lessons.concept: An image either conveys information requiring a text equivalent or is decoration that should remain silent. A table expresses two-dimensional relationships between headers and cells, not arbitrary visual layout. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

explanation.title: Mental model
explanation.text: An image either conveys information requiring a text equivalent or is decoration that should remain silent. A table expresses two-dimensional relationships between headers and cells, not arbitrary visual layout. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

explanation.title: Simple analogy
explanation.text: alt is what you would say over the phone to replace the image; table headers are coordinates for interpreting every value.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: Informative alt describes useful content in context without repeating “image of.” An image already explained nearby or purely decorative receives empty alt. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: width and height reserve aspect ratio before download and prevent layout shift. In Next.js, Image adds optimization and responsive sizes, but alt remains an editorial decision. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: caption names the table; th with scope associates columns or rows. For product cards, use a CSS list rather than table because data does not depend on intersections. blocks.text: An image either conveys information requiring a text equivalent or is decoration that should remain silent. blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: alt is what you would say over the phone to replace the image; table headers are coordinates for interpreting every value.

width and height reserve aspect ratio before download and prevent layout shift. In Next.js, Image adds optimization and responsive sizes, but alt remains an editorial decision. caption names the table; th with scope associates columns or rows. For product cards, use a CSS list rather than table because data does not depend on intersections.
